ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, point $D$ is on $AB$. When folded along $CD$, point $A$ falls on point $E$ on side $BC$. If $\angle B=26^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle CDE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle ACB=90^\circ$ and $\angle B=26^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle A=90^\circ-26^\circ=64^\circ$. \\
By the fold, $\angle CDE=\angle ADC$ and $\angle ACD=\angle BCD=45^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle ADC=180^\circ-45^\circ-64^\circ=71^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle CDE=\angle ADC=\boxed{71^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a folding diagram of a right triangle ABC. C is at the upper left, B is at the lower right, A is at the lower left and is indicated with a dashed line as the position before folding; D is located on the base AB, CD is the crease; A is folded along CD to point E on side BC, in the figure DE is the corresponding line segment after folding, and E is on CB. Reasoning: Because ∠ACB=90°, and ∠B=26°, in triangle ABC ∠A=180°−90°−26°=64°. The folding is carried out along CD, A is reflected to E, and C remains fixed on the crease, so CA is reflected to CE. Also because E is on BC, CE and CB are the same straight line, and the crease CD bisects ∠ACB, giving ∠ACD=∠BCD=45°. Since D is on AB, ∠CAD=∠CAB=64°. In triangle ACD, ∠ADC=180°−45°−64°=71°. The folding also maps DA to DE, while DC remains fixed, so ∠CDE=∠CDA=71°. Final answer: 71°
